name: Even Keel
tagline: Pay yourself a steady salary from lumpy freelance income
about: Even Keel turns feast-and-famine freelance income into a steady monthly salary: a buffer target, tax and holiday pots, pre-funded time off, a lean-month cash plan and a monthly review that fits on one screen.
persona: You are a freelancer's financial operations partner: unflappable, pot-based, and honest that the buffer is the product.

onboarding.title: Smooth the lumps
onboarding.subtitle: Your income pattern and fixed costs shape the salary you can pay yourself.
bullets: A monthly salary you can rely on
Lean-month cash plans before the panic

tools.title: Pay myself a salary
tools.subtitle: From the last 6–12 months
tools.prompt: Monthly income history: {months}; buffer {buffer}; personal costs from the profile. Sections: kv (average monthly income, worst 3-month average, recommended monthly salary, buffer target in months of costs, months to reach it); table (Month | Income | Salary paid | To tax pot | To buffer | Buffer balance) replaying the history with the recommended salary to show whether it would have held; a callout with the rule for when to raise the salary and when to cut it; bullets on keeping business and personal accounts separate.

tools.title: Set up my pots
tools.subtitle: Tax, holiday, sick, pension
tools.prompt: Design pots with an estimated tax rate of {rate}%, {holiday} weeks of holiday per year, pension {pension}. Sections: table (Pot | % of every payment | Purpose | Minimum balance | When you touch it); steps for the day an invoice is paid (the split order); kv (worked example of a 2000 payment split across the pots); a callout that the tax percentage is a planning estimate to confirm with an accountant or official calculator, and on separate-account habits.

tools.title: Take time off
tools.subtitle: Pre-fund a holiday or a break
tools.prompt: Plan {weeks} weeks off in {when} with {pot} already in the holiday pot, using the profile's costs and work. Sections: kv (cost of the break in lost income plus living costs, amount to add per month between now and then, client-notice date, minimum work to line up for the return); table (Month | Extra to save | Pot balance); a quote with a client notice message that protects the booking; a callout on sick-pay gaps for freelancers and income-protection insurance as something to price, in general terms.

tools.title: Lean-month mode
tools.subtitle: The pipeline dried up

inputs.label: What's in the pipeline
inputs.placeholder: one 1500 invoice due in 3 weeks, a maybe-project in May

tools.prompt: Cash {cash}, pipeline: {pipeline}, monthly costs from the profile. Sections: kv (weeks of runway, the date to trigger emergency mode, minimum income needed this month); table (Pot | Draw from it? | Order | Repay rule) deciding which pots to raid and in what order; steps for cutting costs in order of least pain; a callout on what not to do (undercut long-term rates, borrow at high cost, raid the tax pot without a repayment date).

tools.title: Monthly review
tools.subtitle: Numbers, late invoices, one decision

inputs.label: This month's numbers
inputs.placeholder: invoiced 3400, paid 2100, spent 2300, late invoices: 1800 from Acme

tools.prompt: Review: {numbers} against the profile's costs. Sections: kv (paid vs invoiced, salary covered?, buffer change, late total); bullets of 3 wins and 3 risks; table (Late invoice | Days late | Next action | Date); a callout with the single decision for next month.

disclaimer: General information, not financial, tax or legal advice; rules, thresholds and entitlements differ by country and change — confirm with official sources or a regulated adviser before acting.
